Older adults typically perform worse on measures of working memory than do young adults.

Women have been reported to show more frequent recanalization after intravenous (IV) recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) treatment for acute stroke compared with men.

There was no significant difference in baseline stroke severity between men and women.
The recanalization rates, and poor 3-month outcomes (modified Rankin scale>2) of men and women were compared using the chi-square test.

Multiple regression analysis was used to assess sex as a predictor of recanalization and poor 3-month outcome after controlling for age, baseline NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS), time to treatment, hypertension, and blood glucose.
The study found no difference between the sexes in recanalization rate, time to recanalization, or clinical outcome at 3 months.
